text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 8 in history.
1497 - Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama left Lisbon in search of a sea route to India.
1709 - Peter the Great of Russia with 50,000 men defeated Charles XII of Sweden with 20,000 men at the Battle of Poltava. Only 1,500 Swedes escaped and the battle ended Sweden's military might.
1758 - The French under General Montcalm defeated the British under General Abercromby despite superior forces at the battle of Fort Ticonderoga in what now is New York State.
1822 - Percy Bysshe Shelley, English poet, drowned off Leghorn while sailing in the Gulf of Spezia in Italy.
1838 - Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin, builder of rigid airships which are still named after him, born.
1839 - John D. Rockefeller, U.S. oil millionaire and philanthropist, born.
1859 - Oscar I, king of Sweden and Norway, died. King from 1844, he was a liberal reformer early in his reign but after the 1848 revolutions in Europe became more conservative.
1882 - Percy Grainger, American composer born in Australia. Famed for his use of folk-song melodies, he is best remembered for his "Country Gardens" and "Molly on the Shore".
1889 - Jake Kilrain defeated by John L. Sullivan in the last bareknuckle world heavyweight boxing match in Mississippi.
1914 - Billy Eckstine, U.S. jazz singer, born.
1943 - Jean Moulin, hero of the French resistance, died. Known as "Max", he co-ordinated resistance in occupied France but was captured and tortured by the Gestapo and died of his injuries.
1944 - In World War Two, allied naval cruisers and destroyers bombarded Japanese-held Guam.
1967 - British actress Vivien Leigh screen, died; best known for her award winning role in "Gone with the Wind", she also starred in "A Streetcar Named Desire" and "That Hamilton Woman".
1976 - Former President Nixon was disbarred by a New York court after his obstruction of justice during Watergate.
1990 - Albania's communist rulers, rocked by unprecedented public dissent, fired their hardline interior minister and said nearly 5,000 refugees packed into foreign embassies could leave the country.
1992 - Austrian President Kurt Waldheim formally stepped down and was replaced by Thomas Klestil.

1994 - Kim Il-sung, North Korea's authoritarian "Great Leader" since the founding of the Stalinist state in 1948, died of a heart attack. The death of Kim, 82, ended the modern world's longest absolute reign.
1996 - Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan crowned his marathon bid for power with a narrow confidence vote win that shattered secular Turkey's decades-old taboo against political Islam.
1996 - By the narrowest of margins, the International Court of Justice advised that the use or threat of nuclear weapons in war should be outlawed.
